selector.rationale: The presence of a verrucous, exophytic plaque with papillary fronds and nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium, along with mucin-containing goblet cells, supports the diagnosis of Exophytic Schneiderian papilloma.

rejected.label: Inverted papilloma
rejected.why: Inverted papilloma typically presents with an endophytic growth pattern, which contradicts the exophytic nature of the lesion in the vignette.

rejected.label: Squamous papilloma
rejected.why: While squamous papilloma shares some histological features, the presence of mucin-containing goblet cells and the specific growth pattern favor Exophytic Schneiderian papilloma.

rejected.label: Verrucous carcinoma
rejected.why: Verrucous carcinoma is a low-grade malignancy that typically exhibits more pronounced cytologic atypia and invasive growth, which are not present in the vignette.

rejected.label: Squamous cell papilloma
rejected.why: Although it is a close runner-up, the specific combination of histological features, including the presence of mucin-containing goblet cells, makes Exophytic Schneiderian papilloma a more precise diagnosis.
